discovery: Growth of ultra-pure hexagonal boron nitride crystals enabling high-quality van der Waals heterostructures and the physics of two-dimensional quantum materials

nominees.name: Kenji Watanabe
nominees.affiliation: National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS), Tsukuba, Japan

nominees.name: Takashi Taniguchi
nominees.affiliation: National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS), Tsukuba, Japan

motivation: Watanabe and Taniguchi developed high-pressure, high-temperature growth of exceptionally pure hexagonal boron nitride single crystals, establishing hBN as a wide-gap semiconductor with deep-ultraviolet emission and, crucially, as the ideal atomically flat, charge-trap-free dielectric for two-dimensional materials. Encapsulation in their hBN raised graphene mobilities by orders of magnitude and made van der Waals heterostructures a precision platform. Generously supplied to hundreds of laboratories worldwide, these crystals underlie the fractional quantum Hall effect in graphene, Hofstadter's butterfly, magic-angle superconductivity and correlated moire physics, 2D magnetism, and fractional quantum anomalous Hall states. Few contributions have made so much new physics experimentally accessible: an entire generation of discoveries in low-dimensional quantum matter rests on their materials craftsmanship.
